paragraphs.en: “There is one and only one social responsibility of business,” wrote Milton Friedman, a Nobel prize-winning economist, “That is, to use its resources and engage in activities designed to increase its profits.” But even if you accept Friedman’s premise and regard corporate social responsibility (CSR) policies as a waste of shareholders’ money, things may not be absolutely clear-cut. New research suggests that CSR may create monetary value for companies – at least when they are prosecuted for corruption.
paragraphs.zh: 诺贝尔经济学奖得主米尔顿·弗里德曼曾写道：“企业的社会责任有且只有一项，那就是利用其资源，从事旨在增加利润的活动。”但即便你接受弗里德曼的前提，并认为企业社会责任（CSR）政策是在浪费股东的钱，事情也未必如此泾渭分明。新研究表明，履行企业社会责任可能为企业创造经济价值——至少在它们因腐败而被起诉时如此。

paragraphs.en: The largest firms in America and Britain together spend more than $15 billion a year on CSR, according to an estimate by EPG, a consulting firm. This could add value to their businesses in three ways. First, consumers may take CSR spending as a “signal” that a company’s products are of high quality. Second, customers may be willing to buy a company’s products as an indirect way to donate to the good causes it helps. And third, through a more diffuse “halo effect,” whereby its good deeds earn it greater consideration from consumers and others.
paragraphs.zh: 据咨询公司EPG估算，美国和英国的大型企业每年在企业社会责任上的支出，合计超过150亿美元。这可能通过三种方式增加企业价值。第一，消费者可能把企业社会责任支出视为其产品质量上乘的“信号”。第二，顾客可能愿意购买一家公司的产品，以此间接向该公司支持的公益事业捐款。第三，通过更广泛的“光环效应”，公司的善举能够赢得消费者及其他方面更多的体谅和关照。

paragraphs.en: Previous studies on CSR have had trouble differentiating these effects because consumers can be affected by all three. A recent study attempts to separate them by looking at bribery prosecutions under America’s Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA). It argues that since prosecutors do not consume a company’s products as part of their investigations, they could be influenced only by the halo effect.
paragraphs.zh: 以往有关企业社会责任的研究，很难区分这些效应，因为消费者可能同时受到三者的影响。最近的一项研究，试图通过考察依据美国《反海外腐败法》提起的贿赂诉讼，将这些效应区分开来。研究认为，检察官在调查过程中不会把消费公司产品作为调查的一部分，因此他们只可能受到光环效应的影响。

paragraphs.en: The study found that, among prosecuted firms, those with the most comprehensive CSR programmes tended to get more lenient penalties. Their analysis ruled out the possibility that it was firms’ political influence, rather than their CSR stand, that accounted for the leniency: Companies that contributed more to political campaigns did not receive lower fines.
paragraphs.zh: 研究发现，在被起诉的企业中，那些企业社会责任计划最为完善的公司，往往受到更宽大的处罚。研究人员的分析排除了这样一种可能：使企业获得宽大处理的，是其政治影响力，而不是它们在企业社会责任上的立场；因为向政治竞选捐款更多的公司，并未获得较低的罚款。

paragraphs.en: In all, the study concludes that whereas prosecutors should only evaluate a case based on its merits, they do seem to be influenced by a company’s record in CSR. “We estimate that either eliminating a substantial labour-rights concern, such as child labour, or increasing corporate giving by about 20% results in fines that generally are 40% lower than the typical punishment for bribing foreign officials,” says one researcher.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，这项研究得出的结论是：虽然检察官应当仅根据案件本身的事实来评估案情，但他们确实似乎会受到企业履行社会责任记录的影响。一位研究人员说：“我们估计，无论是消除童工之类的重大劳工权利问题，还是把企业捐赠增加约20%，都会使罚款通常比向外国官员行贿所受的典型处罚低40%。”

paragraphs.en: Researchers admit that their study does not answer the question of how much businesses ought to spend on CSR. Nor does it reveal how much companies are banking on the halo effect, rather than the other possible benefits, when they decide their do-gooding policies. But at least they have demonstrated that when companies get into trouble with the law, evidence of good character can win them a less costly punishment.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员承认，他们的研究并未回答企业应该在社会责任方面投入多少资金的问题，也没有揭示企业在决定其行善政策时，有多大程度是在指望光环效应，而不是其他可能的好处。但至少，他们已经证明：当企业惹上法律麻烦时，良好品行的证据可以帮助它们获得代价较小的处罚。
